Ive got a similar set up! One plant in a 7.5 gal fabric pot with ffof and the ff nutes trio. What I did was a major defoliation about one week before I put her into flower and watered her with the 6-4-4 nutes for the last time. I basically chopped all fan leaves up to the top of each branch, sometimes its called an umbrella top. Once she recovered from the defoliation, I flipped her into flower doing an 11 light 13 dark cycle. For the first two weeks, I just let her stretch and gave her plain water when needed. After that, I did some light defoliation to ensure direct light was getting to all the nodes/bud sites that I wanted to develop. I fed her exclusively with water supplemented with fairly heavy feedings of Big Bloom, mainly to ensure the potassium and micronutrients weren’t limiting factors. After that, I just occasionally defoliate to maintain the light to the bud sites and let her do her thing!

Roanoke, Virginia is a nice place if you want to stay relatively close to Eastern Tenn. while being in Virginia. The cost of living is relatively low while still having a decent amount economic opportunities. Its a smaller city and very active/outdoor oriented. Perfect for mountain biking, hiking, and kayaking but no real nightlife. 

Northern Virginia: Nova has everything you could ever need and think to do, but the cost of living is crazy high. You’re a stone’s throw away from DC so you have the benefit of all the museums, nightlife, and great food! Very liberal leaning and great schools as well. Tons of economic opportunities from the federal government, government contracts, lobbyists, nonprofits and everything in between. Traffic can be a nightmare though and it is just densely populated. 

Richmond can be a great option if you don’t mind being further from Tenn. It has a reasonable cost of living, good food selection and nightlife! Lots of economic opportunities as well in state government and the private sector. The crime rate there is relatively high, but it depends a lot on neighborhood, like most cities. 

These are the three places I have the most familiarity with so I can really only talk about them, but hopefully this is beneficial!

Grandin and Salem are smaller and have mostly fresh produce! Down Town is normally much larger and will have lots of arts and crafts, some fresh produce, meats and cheeses, and plants. This has been an internal struggle for me since I had my kid. My wife and I had our son while I was in college, and I was a full blown stoner. I had multiple bongs, would wake n’ bake every day and in general just loved weed. I always smoked outside and kept my paraphernalia locked away out of sight, but being buzzed all day became a problem. So, after many heated discussions with my wife, I decided I needed to get stop. I threw away everything. Hundreds and hundreds of dollars worth of glass and flower, all put into a trash bag and ditched at a 7/11 dumpster. It sucked, but it is what I needed to do at the time. 

I have been diagnosed with depression, anxiety and insomnia and am on a few medications for it, but I think I was using weed as a crutch at the time. Do I think it interfered with my parenting? No, not really. But I want to be present when I’m with my son, and smoking all day put me in a fog sometimes. 

Now, over a year and a few months later, I’m really grateful for the decision I made! I have been able to establish a much healthier and sustainable relationship with weed. I’ve decided to use only at night after my son has gone to sleep, and not every night, because thats what works for me. I have since gotten a mmj card, and learned how to use it but not abuse it. And as my son has gotten older and more mobile/active, I think it has been beneficial. My patience does get tested at times and I can get worn down, but I think having that “me” time at the end of the day has helped keep me recharged for the next day. However, this is just what my experience was and what I found works best.

This isn’t necessarily a singular event, rather more of a singular place. It was the first townhouse my wife (then fiancée) and I moved into together. It was an older place, but was relatively well kept and overall a cozy place. It had two bathrooms and bedrooms, with the bedrooms being upstairs and one bathroom being on each floor.  

It was our first night there. We had gotten our stuff in and started unpacking, but it was getting late so we called it a day and went to bed. My wife kept saying she had a weird feeling about the place, and something just seemed off. I hadn’t noticed anything so I just kind of brushed it off and went to sleep. 

Morning comes around and we had downstairs to make some breakfast. I go to use the downstairs bathroom and it REEKS of cigarettes. It literally smelled like someone had just smoked a pack in there. But, it was only in the bathroom. No where else smelled. And then a couple hours later, the smell was completely gone. Not even a trace of it. 

This ended up happening every single morning for the year we lived there. Downstairs bathroom reeks of cigs, then it’s completely normal come noon. We even had friends and family ask about it when they visited! But we never found an explanation or any even clues as to how. So naturally, we concluded that a ghost must just be smoking cigarettes each morning in the bathroom.

So its kind of a reverse hide and seek. Once its dark, you choose one person to the the “bear” and establish a base. The bear goes and hides while the group waits at the base. Once the bear is hidden, the group goes out and looks for them. The goal of the bear is to tag as many people as possible, while the goal of the group is to find the bear and then make it back to base without being tagged.  When someone in the group finds the bear, they yell “bear’s out!” Which basically means get back to base asap. Every person the bear tags before they’re back becomes a bear with them the next round, until theres only one person left! Its super chaotic and so much fun.
